data.gender_notes: Crispian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name Crispinus, which comes from the Roman god of grain and harvest, Crispus. The name Crispian became popular among Christians due to Saint Crispin, who was a martyr during the Diocletian persecution in the 3rd century. The name Crispian carries the meaning “Ancient Roman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Crispian usually hope their child will grow to embody ancient roman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and resilience in the face of adversity and persecution.
data.etymology: Crispian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ancient Roman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Crispian total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Crispian holds a significant cultural impact by reminding us of the bravery and resilience of early Christian martyrs during the Roman Empire. Saint Crispin, born during the late 2nd or early 3rd century, lived and died for his faith. His story echoes the struggles and sacrifices made by many early Christians in the face of persecution.
data.spiritual_significance: Historically, the name Crispian has a powerful spiritual significance as it represents a deep commitment to faith, even when faced with opposition and persecution. It is a reminder of the steadfastness and unwavering belief in God, even during the most challenging times. It serves as an inspiration for all to remain steadfast in their faith and to follow the example set by the early Christian martyrs.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Crispian is a name derived from Crispus, meaning "golden haired" or "curly-haired" in Latin. Symbolically, it represents the radiant and vibrant spirit of an individual, with a connection to the natural world and its golden hues. Spirually, it suggests the inner fire and brightness of a soul, illuminating the path towards enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Crispian was a martyr in the 3rd century who was converted to Christianity by Saint Alphege. He was a pagan nobleman who was won over by Alphege's teachings and was eventually put to death for his new faith. This event is commemorated on October 25 in the Roman Martyrology.
historical_references.context: Legendary martyr who converted to Christianity under the tutelage of Saint Alphege and was later put to death for his new faith.

historical_references.reference: In the Hagiography of St. Crispin and St. Crispian, written in the 12th century, the two saints Crispin and Crispian are described as brothers and shoemakers who, during the persecutions of Diocletian, were tortured and killed for refusing to abandon their faith. The two saints are considered the patron saints of shoemakers and horsemen.
historical_references.context: Legendary martyrs and shoemakers who were tortured and killed during the persecutions of Diocletian for refusing to abandon their Christian faith.

The name Crispian is derived from the Latin word 'crispus', meaning 'curly-haired'. It was the name of a Christian martyr who was slain on the eve of a pagan festival, the Crispian game, in the late third century AD. Today, the name is seen on LinkedIn profiles of software engineers and developers, GitHub repositories of open-source projects, and Twitter handles of tech influencers and thought leaders.
